nodes.label: VoiceSelector.tsx is dead code: zero production mounts
nodes.norm_label: voiceselector.tsx is dead code: zero production mounts
nodes.description: VERDICT: Dead code, safe to delete. Every VoiceSelector identifier in the repo is self-definition, its own test, one comment in browserSpeechSynthesis.ts:18, research prose (a different repo's file at citation [16]), and 4 plan/RCA docs. Negative results on every mounting mechanism: no .storybook/ directory exists, apps/website has no matches, the complete React.lazy set is enumerated in main.tsx:21-39 and App.tsx:23-39 and VoiceSelector is in none of them, no string-based registry entry, TtsLiveDemoCard.tsx:29-33 imports TtsVoiceProfilePicker and not VoiceSelector, no barrel re-export. Functional risk if deleted: zero for users. tts-single-column-layout.test.ts:39 reads speech.css off disk rather than the component, so it keeps passing after deletion.

nodes.label: VoiceSelector renders ttsVoiceLoading for a permanently empty voice list
nodes.norm_label: voiceselector renders ttsvoiceloading for a permanently empty voice list
nodes.description: VoiceSelector.tsx:61-62 renders t("ttsVoiceLoading") — "Loading system voices…" (i18n/locales/en/extended.ts:2556) — when voices.length === 0, a list that on Linux/WebKitGTK is permanently empty rather than loading. Both live surfaces render ttsVoiceUnavailable instead (TtsVoiceProfilePicker.tsx:104-108, AudioSettingsSection.tsx:712-720). Further proof the component is unmaintained. Six i18n keys are referenced only by this component, and per AGENTS.md rule 6 dead metadata no test reads is a defect, so deletion should take ttsVoiceSelection, ttsVoiceDefault, ttsVoiceDevice, ttsVoiceNetwork, ttsVoiceTest, ttsVoiceTestPreviewTitle, ttsVoiceLoading, ttsVoiceFilterPlaceholder, ttsVoiceFilterSearchAria, ttsVoiceFilterLanguageAria, ttsVoicesAvailableIndonesian and ttsVoicesAvailableNetwork with it.

nodes.label: onChunkTimeout watchdog: specified and ticked complete in the plan, never implemented in code
nodes.norm_label: onchunktimeout watchdog: specified and ticked complete in the plan, never implemented in code
nodes.description: VERDICT: Real gap, should be implemented. The 2026-09-18 Indonesian Google voice profile plan, Task 5 lines 137-151, ticks all four sub-items [x]: add chunkTimeoutMs?: number and onChunkTimeout?: (index: number) => void to ChunkQueueOptions defaulting to Math.max(6000, chunk.length * 80); on timeout clear the pending utterance reference, call window.speechSynthesis.cancel(), emit onChunkTimeout and continue with the next chunk; surface the timeout path in TtsLiveDemoCard via a non-blocking status line. The risk register at :234 lists the hang as a documented Chrome defect and the approval record at :215 lists "chunk watchdog" among approved items. The code has none of it: ChunkQueueOptions (browserSpeechSynthesis.ts:135-143) has exactly seven fields and no timeout fields; speakChunkQueue (:388-403) is a bare sequential for loop whose only exit from chunk i is await this.speak(...); the promise inside speak resolves from exactly two places, utterance.onend and utterance.onerror for canceled/interrupted. This is a plan-checklist integrity failure, not a missing nicety.

nodes.label: Chrome remote Google voices fail to dispatch onstart/onend/error
nodes.norm_label: chrome remote google voices fail to dispatch onstart/onend/error
nodes.description: research/2026-09-18-tts-indonesian-google-voice-profile-deep-research.md:11, citation [12] = code-examples.net "Web Speech API Fix: Chrome Google Voices Not Firing onend/onstart Events" (:46), restated at :31: Chrome has a long-standing defect where remote Google voices fail to dispatch onstart, onend and error, leaving speechSynthesis.speaking stuck true with no audio and no further utterances processed. Users on exactly the voices the feature was built to prefer (Chrome/Edge Google Bahasa Indonesia, network-backed, localService: false) can hit this.

nodes.label: An onend-chained chunk queue wedges permanently when onend never fires
nodes.norm_label: an onend-chained chunk queue wedges permanently when onend never fires
nodes.description: If onend never fires, the await at browserSpeechSynthesis.ts:394 never returns, so speakChunkQueue never reaches :401 and shouldStop is never re-evaluated — the stop-signal guard cannot rescue the queue because the loop is parked inside the await, not at a checkpoint. TtsLiveDemoCard sets status "playing" at :196, the Playing pill at :339-343 is gated on it, and handlePlay early-returns at :193, so the UI shows Playing indefinitely. handleStop (:171-180) does recover the UI — it sets stopRef.current, calls cancel() and unconditionally setStatus("idle") + resetPlaybackState() without awaiting the wedged promise — but cancel() (:420-425) only calls window.speechSynthesis.cancel() and nulls _activeUtterance, so the old speakChunkQueue invocation and its handlePlay closure leak forever, one per stall. The single-chunk path at :241-247 calls speak directly and is more exposed: no queue, no onChunk, no checkpoint at all. _activeUtterance (:158-159) is the anti-GC reference and under a stall it is retained, which is correct for the [12] workaround but never released except by cancel(); the auto-resume at :368-371 repairs a phantom paused engine, not a phantom speaking one, so it cannot break a stall.

nodes.label: ttsVoicePlaybackSkipped copy shipped with no code reading it
nodes.norm_label: ttsvoiceplaybackskipped copy shipped with no code reading it
nodes.description: The decisive evidence that Task 5 was never implemented: ttsVoicePlaybackSkipped exists in both locales (i18n/locales/en/extended.ts:2606 "Skipped a chunk that stopped responding. Try the device voice profile.", id/extended.ts:2639) yet a repo-wide grep finds only those two locale lines and the plan. No component reads it. Task 6 (the copy) was completed; Task 5 (the code the copy describes) was not. This is pending work, not dead code, so the keys must not be deleted. browserSpeechSynthesis.chunk.test.ts:98-136 has exactly 2 speakChunkQueue tests and both stub the thing that would hang (vi.spyOn(...).mockResolvedValue(undefined)) with cancel also mocked — no fake timers, no never-resolving utterance, no stall test, despite the plan's own RED description at :144.

nodes.label: The unmounted-component keep was a deliberate recorded scope decision
nodes.norm_label: the unmounted-component keep was a deliberate recorded scope decision
nodes.description: The three-way duplication was resolved by owner decision and only the profile picker was kept: RCA :91 "TtsLiveDemoCard now mounts only the availability-filtered TtsVoiceProfilePicker; the raw VoiceSelector was removed from the Audio page", RCA :112 "Unused-but-kept per approved scope", progress :68 "| VoiceSelector component file | Keep (unmounted) | Delete component and test | Approved scope said keep available |". nodes.label: Because the queue chains each chunk off the previous onend, a watchdog is a functional requirement
nodes.norm_label: because the queue chains each chunk off the previous onend, a watchdog is a functional requirement
nodes.description: The note's own stated reason, quoted from research :11: Snipset's chunk queue chains each chunk from the previous chunk's onend, so a silent event failure would stall the queue rather than simply truncate audio, which makes a watchdog or timeout guard a functional requirement of the profile feature rather than an optional hardening [15][12]. Without it the headline benefit of the voice-profile work is silently defeated on the platform where the preferred voice is actually available.

nodes.label: Skip-versus-abort on timeout is a product decision because skipping garbles output
nodes.norm_label: skip-versus-abort on timeout is a product decision because skipping garbles output
nodes.description: Watchdog scope and default are a product decision: Math.max(6000, len * 80) and "degrade to the next chunk" versus "abort the whole playback" — silently skipping a chunk produces garbled output, while aborting is louder but safer. The plan chose skip; confirm it still holds now that a fallback-voice policy has since removed fallbacks (availability-rca.md:62).

nodes.label: useTranslation hard default to English
nodes.norm_label: usetranslation hard default to english

nodes.label: useOverlayLanguage localStorage hook
nodes.norm_label: use-overlay-language-localstorage hook
nodes.description: apps/web/src/hooks/useOverlayLanguage.ts:17-20 useOverlayLanguage(): InterfaceLang is the reactive variant. It reads localStorage["snipset-lang"] synchronously, revalidates via get_preferences, and subscribes to the snipset-lang-changed event. The main window writes the key via useAppInitializers.ts:66 persistOverlayLang(lang). utils/overlayLang.ts:10 resolveOverlayLang() is the synchronous one-shot variant, with 3 consumers: features/InputVariableModal.tsx:44, components/MagicMenuNotes.tsx:21, components/MagicMenuNoteInput.tsx:8. The mechanism already existed and was consumed rather than replaced — no new context was created.

nodes.label: Prefer the reactive useOverlayLanguage hook over the one-shot resolveOverlayLang
nodes.norm_label: prefer the reactive useoverlaylanguage hook over the one-shot resolveoverlaylang
nodes.description: Use useOverlayLanguage for components, resolveOverlayLang for module-scope code outside a component; a one-shot read misses a language change that happens after the window opened, which is exactly the bug class being fixed. Outcome across all 17 files in the slice: useOverlayLanguage (reactive) in every one, never resolveOverlayLang, because no file in this slice has module-scope translation code. Four files take lang as a prop instead to keep one IPC read per window (AiSnippetMagicMenuEditingView, SessionList, FloatingSidebarHeader, FloatingSidebarFooter); MfaMagicMenu uses 3 hooks rather than 2 prop interfaces plus 3 call-site edits; FloatingSidebar/index.tsx forwards to 3 children so the read happens once instead of four times.

nodes.label: main.tsx:130 left unpropagated on purpose so a stale one-shot cannot override the reactive value
nodes.norm_label: main.tsx:130 left unpropagated on purpose so a stale one-shot cannot override the reactive value
nodes.description: main.tsx:130 was left untouched deliberately. Passing resolveOverlayLang() there would be a stale one-shot that overrides the reactive value inside ClipboardMagicMenu, because lang ?? overlayLang gives the prop precedence, reintroducing the staleness bug. The reactive in-component fix is strictly better. Consequence accepted and reported: main.tsx stays in the unpropagatedLang ledger with 1 entry. ChatMessages.tsx:132 was not edited by this chunk either; it was fixed by the other chunk mid-session.

nodes.label: RED probe outside the repo
nodes.norm_label: red probe outside the repo
nodes.description: The defect was proven with a throwaway probe under /tmp/opencode/d23b/, never in the repo: symlink src and the repo-root node_modules into the temp dir, write a vitest config with root at apps/web, set localStorage["snipset-lang"] = "id" and have the get_preferences mock return { language: "id" }, then render and show English output. All 18 components rendered English under those conditions across 112 distinct changed t() keys. Dictionary sanity was asserted first: en("copied") = "Copied!" vs id("copied") = "Tersalin!".

nodes.label: An absolute include glob in the vitest config was ignored and started the full 579-file suite
nodes.norm_label: an absolute include glob in the vitest config was ignored and started the full 579-file suite
nodes.description: Reported as a guardrail breach rather than hidden. The first probe config put include as an absolute glob, which vitest ignored, and it began running the full 579-file web suite. It was killed within ~100 s (~623 test files reported) and the config was rebuilt around test.dir so only the probe directory can ever be collected: test.dir set to /tmp/opencode/d23b, test.include = ["*.test.tsx"], root kept at apps/web. No repo change resulted.

nodes.label: The two companion cards need the overlay hook because AICompanionPage never forwards lang
nodes.norm_label: the two companion cards need the overlay hook because aicompanionpage never forwards lang
nodes.description: The two companion cards are in-app, not overlays: they render from pages/AICompanionPage.tsx, which belongs to the other chunk. That page received lang and ignored it via an underscore-prefixed _props discard, and does not forward lang to the cards, so the hook is the only transport available inside this chunk's scope. It resolves correctly because useAppInitializers.ts:66 calls persistOverlayLang(lang) on every change, keeping snipset-lang and snipset-lang-changed in sync in the main window. Follow-up for the owning chunk: pass lang to the two cards and they can drop the hook.
